title: Adobe Names Anil Chakravarthy as Next CEO in Leadership Shift to AI Era
excerpt: The Indian-origin executive will take over as president and CEO on December 1, succeeding Shantanu Narayen after nearly two decades, as Adobe faces mounting competition from AI-native rivals.
body:
• Adobe's board has named Anil Chakravarthy, an Indian-origin executive, as the company's next president and CEO effective December 1, 2026.
  • Outgoing CEO Shantanu Narayen, who led Adobe for nearly two decades, will transition to executive chair.
  • Chakravarthy led Adobe's enterprise business and oversaw AI products including GenStudio and Adobe CX Enterprise.
  • Adobe shares dipped about 1% in after-hours trading amid concerns about competition from AI-native challengers like Canva and Figma.

A New Chapter for Adobe

Adobe announced on Wednesday that Indian-origin executive Anil Chakravarthy will become the company's next president and chief executive officer, effective December 1, 2026. The appointment follows a rigorous search process led by a special committee of Adobe's Board of Directors, according to a company press release.

Shantanu Narayen, who has served as CEO for over 18 years and disclosed plans to step down in March, will transition to executive chair. The two will work closely to ensure a smooth handover, Adobe said.

"I could not be more confident that Anil is the right person to lead Adobe's growth in an AI-driven era and look forward to working closely with him in my new role as executive chair."

— Shantanu Narayen, Adobe Executive Chair

From Informatica CEO to Adobe's Top Job

Chakravarthy joined Adobe in January 2020 to lead its digital experience business and later took on responsibility for the company's worldwide field operations serving enterprise customers. By the end of 2021, he was promoted to president of digital experience and worldwide field operations, according to Reuters.

Before joining Adobe, Chakravarthy spent four years as chief executive of Informatica, the cloud data-management company that was later acquired by Salesforce in an $8 billion deal, according to the Wall Street Journal. At Adobe, he led the development of AI-powered products including GenStudio, Adobe CX Enterprise and Brand Visibility, while also scaling Adobe Experience Platform.

Frank Calderoni, Adobe's lead independent director who oversaw the selection process, said the board "unanimously determined that Anil is the right leader for Adobe's next chapter of growth," citing his track record of "innovation-led growth" over the past six and a half years.

AI Competition Reshapes the Landscape

The leadership transition comes at a pivotal moment for Adobe. The company has been trying to reassure investors concerned about disruptions from rapidly advancing AI technology. Adobe shares have fallen about 18% this year after declining over 21% in 2025, according to Reuters.

Competition is intensifying. Canva has broadened its challenge to professional creative software through its acquisition of Affinity, which it made free. Salesforce is deploying AI agents for marketing and customer engagement. Barron's noted that AI tools such as Claude Design could hurt demand for Adobe's core products.

Adobe has responded by expanding Firefly, its generative AI platform, into more creative workflows and adding AI agents across products including Photoshop and Premiere. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, the company reported record revenue of $6.62 billion, up 13% year on year, with AI-first annual recurring revenue more than tripling to above $500 million, according to YourStory.

Continuing the Indian-Origin Leadership Legacy

Chakravarthy's appointment continues a notable pattern of Indian-origin executives leading major American technology companies. He succeeds Narayen, who joined Adobe in 1998 and transformed the company from a desktop software maker into a cloud-subscription powerhouse with a portfolio spanning creative tools, document management and digital customer experiences.

Adobe also faces the departure of finance chief Dan Durn, who left in June, adding to uncertainties until a permanent successor is named. The company reports earnings next week.

What Comes Next

Chakravarthy signalled his focus on "agentic software" — tools that carry out multi-step tasks rather than responding to individual commands. "I'm energized by the opportunity to fuel growth and drive Adobe's leadership in the next era of agentic software for creativity, productivity and customer experience," he said. In the European Union, the AI Act's broad applicability as of August 2 adds another regulatory dimension for Adobe, whose products increasingly generate and modify media.
